# UI Visual Design

Use this skill when the main problem is visual clarity: hierarchy, layout, spacing, scanability, emphasis, or redesigning weak screen structure.

## When to Use

- Improve a cluttered or confusing screen
- Redesign weak card, dashboard, form, or navigation layouts
- Strengthen hierarchy and primary action clarity
- Tune spacing, grouping, and emphasis without changing core product behavior

## Workflow

### 1. Identify the Main Visual Job

- Determine what the user should notice first, second, and third
- Identify the primary action and any distracting secondary content
- Preserve strong existing patterns and redesign only weak or confusing areas

### 2. Build Hierarchy

- Use headings, sectioning, spacing, and emphasis to create a readable flow
- Group related content and separate unrelated controls
- Avoid giving equal visual weight to everything on the screen

### 3. Improve Scanability

- Prefer short labels and compact supporting text
- Use lists, cards, tables, and panels only when they help comprehension
- Reduce noise before adding new decorative treatment

### 4. Make Actions Clear

- Keep one dominant action per major surface where possible
- Distinguish destructive, secondary, and passive actions clearly
- Place actions close to the content they affect

### 5. Review for Consistency

- Compare spacing, alignment, and typography with nearby screens
- Keep the existing product language where it works
- Redesign weak visual patterns instead of copying them forward

## Completion Checks

- The primary action is visually obvious
- The layout is easy to scan
- Related content is grouped coherently
- Weak hierarchy has been improved, not preserved

## Prompt Starters

- Use ui-visual-design to redesign this dashboard for stronger hierarchy and less clutter
- Use ui-visual-design to improve the spacing and action clarity of this form page
